key_insight: The paper shows that small open-source multimodal agents can become much better at GUI task planning by learning from their own autonomous exploration and from hindsight-style experience reuse. In simple terms: instead of relying only on labeled demos, the agent teaches itself how to plan across different websites.
problem_solved: Current multimodal web agents often struggle with long-horizon planning and do not generalize well across websites. This is especially problematic for smaller open-source MLLMs, which are cheaper and more private but have weaker planning abilities than large commercial models.
method: Introduces Planning Experience Exploration and Utilization (PEEU), a self-improvement framework for GUI agents.
Autonomously explores environments to collect planning experiences without requiring extensive manual annotation.
Uses hindsight experience utilization to recycle and reinterpret past interactions into useful planning supervision for better generalization.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to improve web and GUI agents without depending heavily on expensive labeled data or proprietary models. It is especially relevant for building cost-efficient, privacy-preserving agents that need to work reliably across many websites.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing exploration -> experience collection -> hindsight reuse -> improved task planning
Before/after comparison of small MLLM planning performance with and without PEEU
Icon set for web browser, task decomposition, and memory/experience replay
Flowchart illustrating cross-website generalization on repetitive GUI tasks
paper_title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
paper_authors: Tianyi Men, Zhuoran Jin, Pengfei Cao, Yubo Chen, Kang Liu
